test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 27 Dec, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: How does a plant move its leaves in response to touch?

options.text: By changing the amount of water in them
By changing the amount of protein in them
By changing the amount of nucleic acid in them
By changing the amount of lipid in them

solution:
The correct answer is __**By changing the amount of water in them**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Plants such as the Mimosa pudica move their leaves in response to touch through changes in turgor pressure, which is the pressure of water inside the plant cells.
 
• Turgor pressure is controlled by the movement of water into and out of the cells in the pulvini, which are the swollen bases of the leaf stalks.
 
• When touched, the cells on the inner side of the pulvini lose water and shrink, causing the leaves to fold.
 
• This rapid movement is an example of a nastic movement, which is a non-directional response to a stimulus.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Turgor Pressure:** The force within the cell that pushes the plasma membrane against the cell wall, crucial for maintaining the plant's structure and function.
 
• **Pulvini:** Specialized motor organs at the base of a leaf or leaflet that facilitate movement through changes in turgor pressure.
 
• **Nastic Movements:** Non-directional responses to stimuli, such as the folding of leaves in response to touch or light changes.
 
• **Mimosa pudica:** A plant species known for its rapid leaf movements in response to touch, commonly referred to as the "sensitive plant" or "touch-me-not."
 
• **Hydraulic Mechanism:** The process involving water movement within plant cells that enables quick movements such as the folding of leaves in response to touch.
